newsitem.title: USA: Well funded int'l capital marts a priority - Summers.
newsitem.headline: Well funded int'l capital marts a priority - Summers.

text.p: Creating a well-funded global capital market is a key part of the U.S. strategy to promote worldwide growth and stability, Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said Thursday.

"At Treasury, our most crucial international priority remains the creation of a well funded truly global capital market," Summers said at a forum sponsored by the Brookings Institution, a Washington research group.
"When other countries grow more rapid, they buy more of our products, produce better goods for us to buy and cooperate on global objectives," he said.

Calling the work of development banks critical for the majority of the world's nations that cannot attract large-scale private investment, Summers said the resources of those institutions will have to be used more creatively.

"As private markets take on more functions that development banks once performed, these energies can be channeled to meeting social concerns," Summers said in the text of his speech which was released by the Treasury Department.

In his wide-ranging speech on integrating national economies, Summers also said the United States would promote open markets by working to deepen the effectiveness of the World Trade Organization, participate in regional trade arrangements and unilaterally promote measures that would "insure that markets are opened."

"The United States' economic policy should and will be based on the idea that promoting integration and prosperity around the world is enormously in our national interest -- enormously in our national interest because of the stability it brings in a world that is still a dangerous place," he said.
